title: The Small Voice with a Good Idea

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 6-12)

collection.description: A child tells an adult the pigs dig under the fence, not over it: try the child's idea, or do it the grown-up way.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The pigs keep getting out, and the adults have been arguing for a week about how to fix the fence. (friend) has been listening from a tree. Today (friend.he/she) climbs down and tells (subject), "The pigs dig under. They don't go over. The fence needs to go DOWN, not up."

choices.label: Thank (friend.him/her) and Do It the Grown-Up Way

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) blinks. Then (subject.he/she) looks at the fence. There are dig marks under it. Lots of them. (subject) sinks the bottom of the fence a hand deep into the earth. The pigs stay in. "Who thought of that?" asks somebody at the fire. "(friend)," says (subject). (friend) pretends not to be pleased. (friend.He/she) is extremely pleased.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) thanks (friend) and builds the fence taller, as the adults agreed. The pigs dig under it the next night. (subject) stands there looking at the hole for a long time. Then (subject.he/she) goes to find (friend) and asks (friend.him/her) to explain it again, slowly. (friend) does, with great patience.
